newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks surge to end at day's highs.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks surge to end at day's highs.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed with a sharp rebound Tuesday, driven by hopes Congress will speed up debate of tax reforms, dealers said.
"This is a counter-trend movement on strictly local factors, namely a better scenario for approval of the tax package which could fuel new gains tomorrow," said Jorge Bonanno at Interfin brokers.
The blue-chip MerVal index jumped 3.4 percent to close at session highs of 514.64, after falling slightly Monday and tumbling 4.7 percent last week despite a strong rise Friday.
Traders said the recovery, which pared MerVal losses to 2.7 percent so far in August, was aided by end-of-month position squaring.

"The combination of good news capping a month with a negative trend is bound to trigger off a technical rally," said Bonanno, predicting the MerVal could climb to 533 in the near-term before pulling back.

Analysts welcomed earlier comments by deputy Oscar Lamberto, head of the lower house budget committee, who forecast the package of tax hikes and other austerity measures would pass Congress virtually unchanged.

"We're feeling the consensus, it's starting to take shape and we can probably expect a vote mid-September -- last week it seemed Congress would drag its feet until October," said an analyst at a U.S.-based investment bank.

The measures, announced two weeks ago with the aim of plugging a fiscal hole, are considered a key test for Economy Minister Roque Fernandez, who was unexpectedly named to replace Domingo Cavallo July 26.
In the session the broad market index jumped 3.1 percent, with winners outstripping losers 39 to 10 and 15 stocks closing flat.

Floor volume remained extremely weak at 13.1 million pesos but more than doubled from a 10-month low of 6.1 million recorded Monday. Over-the-counter deals swelled to 89.6 million pesos from 42.5 million Monday.
Top main-tier performers were construction stock Polledo, carmaker Sevel and Telefonica, which shot up 6.8 percent, 6.5 percent and 6.1 percent, respectively.
The only MerVal loser was pulp and paper maker Celulosa, off 1.2 percent.
